messages.text: New review came in, deal with it - not much to do, we should be able to sign this off very soon.
I’ll read the new review, address the remaining points, and update PR #4. I’ll keep any final sign-off with the human reviewer.

Most points are now agreed. The remaining change is a more generous, justified space reservation for a 3 T central solenoid; detailed magnet and muon design should stay in the next research step.

I’ll also record the requested baseline choices: retain the aggressive 25 mm tracker envelope, investigate the outermost tracker layer for timing, and plan ACTS-based propagation in the software stack.

The space budget now reserves 400 mm radially for the solenoid assembly, including cold mass, cryostat interfaces and integration margin, plus end allowances. I’ve moved the adjacent calorimeter envelopes outward and downstream to accommodate it while retaining their nominal depths and gaps.

The regenerated drawing has no overlapping allocation boxes. This gives us a justified planning allowance for the envelope review; detailed magnet feasibility remains part of the next study.

PR #4 now contains the revised space budget, updated drawing and replies to the remaining substantive comments. The checks passed: 26 tests, 24 session records validated, and no overlapping allocation rectangles.

The proposal is ready for human review of the envelope baseline. Detailed magnetic-field and muon-system research remains the next step.

Updated [PR #4](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/4) and answered the remaining substantive comments.

- Added an explicit **400 mm solenoid space budget** for the 3 T hypothesis.
- Adjusted neighbouring envelopes and regenerated the drawing.
- Recorded the agreed tracker, timing and forward-calorimeter baseline choices.
- Kept detailed magnet/muon research for the next step.

**Checks:** 26 tests passed; no overlapping allocation rectangles; working tree clean.

DES-003 and ADR-006 are ready for human envelope review/sign-off. The magnet allowance remains a planning estimate, not engineering certification.
